messages:
mia-support: Hey team, escalating a customer ticket—they saw intermittent 500s on the /v1/generate endpoint and are missing audit logs for 2026-03-08 02:00-03:30 UTC. Customer is asking for ISO evidence on log retention + KMS/HSM handling. Repro included below.

jake-privacy: Thanks. Can you drop the support ticket ID and the exact request-id(s)? Also need to know whether the payloads were stored in raw logs or only metadata.

mia-support: Ticket #CS-12842. Sample request-id: req_7a9c5f2b. Repro steps:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -H "X-Request-ID: req_7a9c5f2b" \
  -d '{"prompt":"test"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
# Response: HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error\n# {"error":"internal_server_error","trace":"trace-9f2b"}
```

Customer reports no audit entries in our audit-log index for that request-id during that window.

anna-security: Acknowledged. I'll pull key usage logs and audit-log ingestion for that timeframe. Which environment (prod/us-west-2 or eu-west-1)? Customer is EU-based.

mia-support: eu-west-1.

leo-sre: Quick check — can you paste the exact timestamp when you saw the 500? I'll grep ELK and S3. For quick repro of logs we use: 
```
# internal helper to fetch indexed audit logs
./tools/query_audit --env eu-west-1 --q "request_id:req_7a9c5f2b" --from 2026-03-08T02:00Z --to 2026-03-08T03:30Z
```

jake-privacy: For ISO mapping: we need to know where the audit trail artifacts live (ELK index name, S3 bucket keys) and the retention period enforced (e.g., 90 days) so we can map to controls A.12.4, A.18.1. Also confirm encryption at rest: CMK in HSM or customer-managed?

olivia-compliance: I can update the control matrix once we have the artifact names and retention SLA. Please include exact proof artifacts (screenshot of retention policy, S3 lifecycle rule id, KMS key alias) — that'll be what auditors want.

anna-security: Found ingestion logs: there was a short pipeline backpressure at 2026-03-08T02:12:40Z causing ~3% drop in audit ingestion. Request req_7a9c5f2b appears in the raw proxy logs but failed to index due to a transient ES rejection. I'm extracting the raw event and KMS envelope logs now. KMS key alias used for audit-s3 is alias/redwood-audit-cmk (account-managed CMK rotated every 365d via KMS Automatic Rotation).

leo-sre: I pulled the raw proxy line and the ELK error: 
```
[2026-03-08T02:12:40Z] req_7a9c5f2b - upstream error 500 - backend-timeout
elasticsearch: rejected_execution_exception: rejected queue full
```
I also fetched the S3 object for that day's batched archive: s3://redwood-audit-archive/eu-west-1/2026/03/08/02-12-archive.json.gz (object exists).

mia-support: Nice. Customer specifically asked whether payloads are retained and whether we store any unencrypted request bodies. Need a short plain-language answer for them.

jake-privacy: Plain answer: request/response payloads are captured in the proxy logs as metadata only by default; full request bodies are only stored if ingestion rule enabled for debugging or if the user opted into request logging. All stored artifacts are encrypted at rest using account CMKs (alias/redwood-audit-cmk) and we use HSM-backed key material. We will confirm the exact lifecycle rule.

olivia-compliance: For the ISO artifact pack I need: 1) S3 lifecycle rule id (to show 90d retention), 2) screenshot of KMS key rotation settings or KMS key policy, 3) ELK index retention policy (ILM) name and snapshot schedule.

anna-security: Attached extracts (pasted below):
- KMS alias: alias/redwood-audit-cmk
- Key rotation: enabled, rotate_every_days=365
- S3 lifecycle rule id: audit-retention-rule-90d
- ILM policy: audit-logs-ilm-90d
- Evidence location: s3://redwood-compliance-evidence/CS-12842/ (will stage the files there)

leo-sre: Repro steps I ran to fetch the raw event: 
```
# fetch archived batch from S3 and search for request id
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-audit-archive/eu-west-1/2026/03/08/02-12-archive.json.gz - | zgrep req_7a9c5f2b
# query ELK
curl -s -u svc-audit:REDACTED "https://elk.eu-west-1.redwood/_search?q=request_id:req_7a9c5f2b&pretty" | jq '.hits.hits[] | {index: ._index, _source: ._source}'
```

mia-support: Great — I'll send the customer a summarized note: include that the request was captured in proxy logs and archived batch, indexing dropped due to transient ES rejection, retention is 90 days, artifacts encrypted with alias/redwood-audit-cmk (CMK rotated annually), and we've staged evidence in s3://redwood-compliance-evidence/CS-12842/.

olivia-compliance: I'll take those artifacts and update the ISO 27001 mapping sheet (control references A.12.4, A.10.1 for crypto, A.18.1 for compliance evidence). Will attach the updated matrix to the ticket and CC customer.

deploy-bot: Deploy finished: runtime/elk-pipeline v3.2.1 promoted to prod at 2026-03-09T05:00Z (notes: backpressure mitigations). :white_check_mark:

anna-security: As a follow-up action, I'll open an RCA ticket for the ES rejection and schedule an ILM review to ensure archive indexing is retried. ETA to customer evidence: 48 hours.

mia-support: Thanks team — passing to CS to send to customer. Marking as escalated->security.

jake-privacy: Small note for the response: add that EU-regulated data handling is aligned with our Data Processing Addendum and we will provide hashes of archived artifacts rather than full payloads if customer requests minimization.

mia-support: Noted. I'll include that option. Closing the Slack thread here, will update CS-12842 when evidence is uploaded. :handshake:
